title: Hybrid metaheuristic optimization of convolutional neural networks for tomato leaf disease classification
task: Hyperparameter optimization for CNN-based plant disease classification
key_results: ALO-DA hybrid metaheuristic achieved 97.83% test accuracy on tomato leaf disease dataset (21,421 training images, 10 classes); hybrid approaches outperformed single optimizers
comments: While hyperparameter tuning via metaheuristics is practical, the fixed CNN architecture limits generalizability of findings across different model designs.

inputs: tomato leaf images (21,421 training, 4,586 validation, 4,602 test)
CNN architecture with tunable dropout and learning rate

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hybrid metaheuristics balance exploration and exploitation better than single optimizers for CNN hyperparameter tuning
hypotheses.result: ALO-DA, ALO-WOA, and PSO-WOA achieved higher accuracy (97.52–97.83%) than ALO-PSO (95.26%)

title: Spatial scaling of metagenomic diversity reveals ecological disruption in the gut microbiome of gout patients
task: Characterizing gut microbiome dysbiosis in gout via metagenomic diversity scaling
key_results: Gout microbiomes showed higher inter-individual dissimilarity in rare genes (z-values), weaker scaling of dominant genes, and substantially reduced maximal accrual diversity compared to healthy controls; perturbed functional gene cluster scaling
comments: The m-DAR model provides novel ecological perspective on dysbiosis, but translation to clinical microbiome-based therapeutics remains speculative and requires validation.

inputs: gut microbiome samples from gout patients and healthy controls
outputs: diversity scaling parameters (z-values), maximal accrual diversity (MAD), functional gene cluster scaling

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gout dysbiosis manifests as altered ecological structure with reduced homogeneity in dominant taxa and constrained diversity potential
hypotheses.result: Gout microbiomes exhibited higher rare gene diversity scaling, lower dominant gene scaling, and reduced MAD compared to controls

hypotheses.hypothesis: Functional pathways are differentially perturbed in gout microbiomes
hypotheses.result: Increased CAZy scaling but decreased KEGG/KO pathway scaling in gout samples

title: SwiftMSeg: lightweight multi-scale local–global context modeling with transformer for medical image segmentation
task: Lightweight medical image segmentation with multi-scale context modeling
key_results: SwiftMSeg achieved Dice scores of 0.896 (colonoscopy), 0.860 (pathology), 0.850 (ultrasound), 0.870 (MRI) with only 4.48M parameters (~53× fewer than U-Net); statistically significant improvements (p < 0.001)
comments: Exceptional parameter efficiency and cross-modal generalization, though moderate external dataset performance suggests domain adaptation remains a challenge.

model_io.model: SwiftMSeg (convolutional encoder + transformer local-global-local module + hierarchical decoder)
outputs: segmentation masks for anatomical structures (nuclei, polyps, tumors)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combining multi-scale refinement with transformer-based global context modeling improves boundary localization and contextual accuracy
hypotheses.result: Lower Hausdorff distance (16.43 MRI, 33.89 ultrasound) and reduced asymmetric surface distance compared to baselines

title: Hybrid CNN BiLSTM architecture for smart grid cyberattack detection using smart meter data
task: Real-time cyberattack intrusion detection in smart grids via CNN–BiLSTM–ExtraTrees ensemble on meter data
key_results: CNN–BiLSTM–ExtraTrees achieved 92.17% accuracy, 90.58% precision, 81.24% recall, 85.66% F1, 95.60% ROC-AUC with 12 ms inference latency on 72,073 labeled power-grid logs across 5 attack types
comments: Comprehensive evaluation including imbalance-handling strategies, ablation studies (20.12 pp gain from bidirectionality), and statistical testing (McNemar p<0.001); addresses practical deployment constraints effectively.

model_io.model: CNN–BiLSTM–ExtraTrees with attention and class weighting
inputs: 128-dimensional smart meter measurements (voltage, current, frequency harmonics, multi-modal)
high-frequency time series of meter data

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bidirectional temporal modeling captures attack-evolution patterns better than unidirectional processing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: BiLSTM increased accuracy by 20.12 pp over unidirectional CNN-LSTM

hypotheses.hypothesis: ExtraTrees ensemble head provides more robust decisions than Softmax for class-imbalanced cyber-attack data
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ExtraTrees boosted precision by 10.09 pp over standalone baseline

hypotheses.hypothesis: Weighted-learning strategy optimally balances class imbalance (2.49:1 ratio) compared to SMOTE variants
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: weighted learning identified as Pareto-optimal choice via comprehensive comparative study against 9 imbalance-handling strategies

title: A fractal-enhanced deep learning framework for forecasting agricultural production in India
task: Agricultural production forecasting via fractal-enhanced LSTM/Bi-LSTM
key_results: LSTM with variable-scaling FIF achieved MAPE of 1.70% (Wheat), 1.95% (Maize), 5.06% (Millet); Bi-LSTM achieved 1.39% (Rice); Hurst exponent 0.777–0.875 with variable scaling
comments: Strong empirical results on a real agricultural dataset, though comparison to non-fractal baselines and statistical significance testing (Wilcoxon, Diebold–Mariano) strengthen claims; fractal augmentation appears domain-beneficial for volatile time series.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Variable-scaling FIF produces rougher interpolation that better captures non-smooth features than constant-scaling FIF
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: variable-scaling FIF yielded lower Hurst exponent (0.777–0.875) and higher fractal dimension (1.153–1.574), improving model performance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fractal interpolation improves recurrent network learning on agricultural time series
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: models trained on fractal-interpolated data significantly outperformed those on original data across three of four crops

title: A novel hybrid intelligent optimization strategy for multi-objective trajectory planning of robotic arms in precision assembly scenarios
task: Multi-objective robotic arm trajectory planning via improved CEMOPSO for precision assembly
key_results: CEMOPSO increased assembly efficiency by 15.2%, reduced energy consumption by 20.4%, decreased impact by 26.4% versus baseline on pyrotechnic grain assembly task
comments: Real engineering validation is valuable, but quantitative comparisons against other multi-objective optimizers and statistical testing are absent; improvements are substantial but generalization to other assembly tasks unclear.

inputs: precision assembly task parameters (time, energy, mechanical impact constraints)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Chebyshev mapping and evolutionary elimination improve MOPSO performance for assembly
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: CEMOPSO outperformed baseline in efficiency, energy, and impact metrics on pyrotechnic grain assembly

title: A staged vision-force collaborative framework for precision robotic insertion of metallic valve components
task: Vision–force collaborative robotic insertion of metallic valve components via staged sensing-reliability handover
key_results: SVFC improved insertion success rate, reduced insertion time, and lowered peak contact forces versus baseline methods on clearance-fit and interference-fit tasks
comments: Well-motivated staged framework addressing real physical challenges (specular reflection, depth loss), but quantitative metrics (success rate %, time reduction, force reduction) are stated qualitatively without numerical values or statistical analysis.

model_io.model: SVFC (vision-force collaborative controller with spiral trajectory + variable-parameter admittance)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Staged handover from vision-dominant alignment to force-dominant contact regulation reduces insertion failure and contact trauma
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: SVFC improved success rate, time, and peak forces on representative clearance/interference-fit tasks versus baseline

title: Calibration method for the optical system of infrared CMOS-theodolite in astronomical measurement
task: High-precision optical calibration for infrared CMOS-theodolite astronomical measurement system
key_results: Daytime RMSE ≤ 0.33″ longitude, 0.34″ latitude; nighttime RMSE ≤ 0.26″ longitude, 0.29″ latitude; method achieves stably calibrated parameters for low-resolution CMOS sensors
comments: Innovative two-face measurement calibration approach addresses practical constraints of removed eyepiece and small field-of-view, with robust all-weather validation demonstrating operational maturity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Two-face angle measurement provides sufficient constraints for precise principal point determination despite low pixel resolution
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; achieved sub-arcsecond RMSE (0.26–0.34″) in both daytime and nighttime conditions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Method generalizes across diverse observational environments (daytime/nighttime)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; nighttime measurements slightly more accurate (0.26–0.29″) than daytime (0.33–0.34″)

title: Optical vortex transfer and dispersion-controlled light propagation in an Er³⁺: YAG three-level quantum system
task: Coherent orbital-angular-momentum transfer and dispersion control in Er³⁺:YAG
key_results: Complete OAM transfer with topological-charge preservation; optimal Er³⁺ concentration of 3% maximizes vortex-transfer efficiency
comments: Solid theoretical and numerical framework using density-matrix formalism, though experimental validation of the concentration-dependent efficiency optimization would strengthen claims.

model_io.model: Coupled Maxwell–Bloch equations with density-matrix formalism

hypotheses.hypothesis: Sum-frequency nonlinear process transfers OAM with concentration-dependent efficiency
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 3% Er³⁺ concentration optimal; complete phase and topological-charge preservation observed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Absorption and dispersion spectra indicate fast/slow propagation regimes selectable by concentration
hypotheses.result: Supported; concentration-selectable transitions demonstrated through spectral analysis

title: Investigation of vorticity and secondary flow strength near the protected bridge pier in a sharp bend
task: Characterization of vorticity and secondary flow around bridge pier in sharp bends
key_results: Peak vorticity observed at 84° section (counterclockwise); peak secondary flow strength at 70° section with 3 mm collar; 30% reduction in secondary flow strength when collar thickness increased from 0.06b to 0.24b
comments: Practical engineering study with direct relevance to pier design, though the physical mechanisms explaining the non-monotonic secondary flow behavior between 70–80° warrant deeper theoretical investigation.

model_io.model: 180° bend-shaped channel with oblong pier and variable collar

inputs: probe beam focusing at measurement points

hypotheses.hypothesis: Collar thickness reduces pier-induced secondary circulation strength
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; increasing thickness from 0.06b to 0.24b reduced peak secondary flow strength by ~30%

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pressure gradient and secondary flow intensity vary with bend position
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; peak tangential velocity near convex bank; non-monotonic secondary flow variation between 70–80° bend angles
